This design doc outlines the plan for a QTD1/3 combination, which will have a Shiny app frontend and have incremental development steps.

## Motivation

-   The current QTD1 app is not working correctly anymore (reproducibility issues).
-   The IT security department does not like the fact that the QTD1 and QTD3 apps are installed on desktop computers directly, instead of being hosted on a server, due to the Java implementation.
-   Both the `gsbDesign` and `BinaryTrial` R packages which are the foundation of the QTD3 app are not maintainable due to their complexity and structure, and therefore should not be used as a basis for the new QTD1/3 combination app.
-   The R package `RBeST` should be considered as a potential basis for the Bayesian part.
-   Development should be incremental, starting with the QTD1 functionality and a slimmed down Bayesian design functionality without interim analyses for the QTD3 part. Extensions must be possible, e.g. for adding interim analyses, meta-analytic-predictive (MAP) mixture priors, etc.

## Objectives

Develop a Shiny app that replicates the fixed design functionality (no interims) of QTD1 (frequentist part) and QTD3 (Bayesian part):

-   Include continuous and binary endpoints.
-   When a user requests it, the system must generate and display the R code that was executed - showing exactly how their inputs are applied and how each output is produced. 
    - Note: In `rpact`, we leverage the existing function `getObjectRCode()` to retrieve the full underlying code for any object, so we can reuse this functionality directly rather than implementing it from scratch when adding the *QTD1 part* to the `rpact` R package.
-   The underlying computations shall be implemented in open source R packages, that can also be used without the Shiny app.
    -   The names of quantities etc should be based on the @lalonde2007 paper instead of on the QTD1 app, to be easily useable by external users too.
-   Follow good software engineering practices, in particular the [`openstatsguide`](https://openstatsware.org/guide.html).
-   The Shiny app must offer users the option to copy the exact R code used for calculations to their clipboard - so they can seamlessly incorporate it into their own analyses on a validated R installation
    - Note: When integrated into RPACT Cloud, we provide a Download Report feature that lets them export the complete code (as Rmd, qmd, and R scripts) along with rendered outputs (HTML, PDF), or have everything sent to them via email.
-   The Shiny app must have the option for the user to copy the R code used for the calculations to the clipboard, so that it can be used in their own analyses on a validated R installation.

## Proposal

-   Develop the calculations for the *QTD1 part* in the `rpact` R package
    -   It fits within the scope of the package because `rpact` includes fixed design analyses and operating characteristics
    -   In terms of additional statistical methods, little will be needed (maybe score test based confidence intervals for binary proportions)
    -   The code will be automatically included in the validation process of the `rpact` package
    -   Open source available on CRAN as part of `rpact`
-   Perform the calculations for the *QTD3 part* with the `RBeST` R package by @weber2021
    -   In `RBesT` the decision functions can be set up to require that multiple critical probability thresholds and quantiles for the difference distribution have to be met in the two-sample case while these thresholds are applied directly to the posterior density in the one-sample case. 
    -   This enables evaluation of so-called dual criterion designs which evaluate a statistical confidence criterion (high confidence in a positive/negative difference) and a minimally observed treatment difference (observed median difference being greater/smaller than some value), which is what is needed for the QTD app.
    -   Note that for the fixed design functionality, the `RBeST` package would not really be needed, because the calculations can be done eventually with the `rpact` package. However, this will provide a good starting point for the future extension to meta-analytic-predictive (MAP) mixture priors.
    -   It would seem easiest to contribute to `RBeST` where possible, and have additional layering/interface functionality in the Shiny app where needed (e.g. logic to create R code for copy/paste, etc.)
    -   Also we would like to highlight that we would not provide validation documentation for the `RBeST` package, because it is maintained by Novartis colleagues and not by RCONIS
-   Develop the *Shiny app* to be a new module of the RPACT Cloud
    -   Code would not be public, but free usage up to certain usage limit for the public
    -   The app would be hosted on the RPACT Cloud, see [here](https://cloud.rpact.com)
    -   Installation as part of RPACT Cloud in Novartis internally, easily available for everyone in the existing RPACT Cloud deployment, deployment instructions and source code available in the Novartis-specific GitHub repository, see [here](https://github.com/rpact-com/rpact.cloud.novartis)
    -   By integrating QTD into RPACT Cloud, you instantly gain a suite of powerful features at no extra development cost - everything from one-click R-code export and “Download Report” (Rmd, qmd, R script + rendered HTML/PDF) to automated email delivery is available out of the box. What’s more, we’re currently building a bookmarking feature that lets you save and reload entire design objects via a shareable URL or an RDS file - and as soon as it ships, QTD users will benefit from it too.

## Estimated effort

Here we give a rough estimate of the effort needed for the work packages above. Note that these are rough and conservative estimates, using an assumption of 4 hours of productive and focused work per day.

- `rpact` extensions for QTD1 calculations: 15 days
  - Methodology review and specification: 2 days
  - Prototype development: 3 days
  - Package development: 3 days
  - Vignettes and examples: 2 days
  - Validation documentation: 3 days
  - Release on CRAN: 2 days
- `RBeST` usage for QTD3 calculations: 13 days
  - Methodology review and specification: 2 days
  - Prototype development: 3 days
  - Vignette documenting the usage: 3 days
  - Comparison with existing `gsbDesign` and `BinaryTrial` results: 3 days
  - Release on CRAN: 2 days
- RPACT Cloud module with Shiny app: 30 days
  - Wireframe UI: 2 days
  - Prototype development: 10 days
  - Package development: 10 days
  - Integration tests vs. existing QTD1 and QTD3 app results: 5 days
  - Release on GitHub: 3 days

Overall this would be about 58 days of work, or about 232 hours of work assuming 4 hours of productive and focused work on this project per day. We expect that both Daniel and Friedrich would work on this together as a team, which could reduce the calendar timeline. In particular, we would be able to achieve a reimplementation of the fixed designs QTD1/3 app by Q4 of 2025.

## Iterative development approach

As with our other software projects for Novartis, the work will be done in an iterative and incremental way, with regular feedback loops and adjustments based on frequent Novartis feedback. For example, before the final decision to integrate QTD into the RPACT Cloud, we will provide a wireframe UI design such that Novartis can provide feedback on the look and feel.

The initial implementation will focus on the core functionality of QTD1 and a slimmed down version of QTD3 without interim analyses. However, the packages and Shiny app will be designed in a way that future extensions are possible, e.g.:

-   Adding interim analyses to the QTD3 part
-   Adding meta-analytic-predictive (MAP) mixture priors to the QTD3 part
